piece_type: DTC sponsored TV talk-show segment video (celebrity spokesperson; ABC's The View, also YouTube)

cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “. . . something that works in about 15-30 minutes . . .” | “It literally works within, for me, 15 minutes. And anyone with a migraine, for 15 minutes, of pure agony, they’re like knives in my head. So to have this relief, and to not be in a fog afterwards . . . I’m able to just go with the rest of my day.”
cases.context: Co-primary endpoints measured at 2 hours; no prespecified endpoints at 15 or 30 minutes; 'TREATMENT RESULTS MAY VARY' SUPER does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Spokesperson experience does not support onset claims not shown in trials.
cases.check: Rule: flag onset-of-action time claims (minutes/hours) and verify against PI endpoint timepoints.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “I have been on handfuls of different prescriptions and over-the-counter medications, and none of them have really worked for me. Or if they worked, and maybe it was a one or two time thing and then they didn’t work consistently after that. And I was given Nurtec ODT, I tried it, it was a gamechanger[.]” | “So to have this relief, and to not be in a fog afterwards, to not like, other medications would give me rebound headaches, and this one doesn’t . . .”
cases.rationale: Implies superiority over other Rx/OTC products and significant advance ('gamechanger') not demonstrated.
cases.check: Does a testimonial imply superiority or a breakthrough ('gamechanger') versus other treatments?

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: Interview portion communicates Nurtec ODT is for the treatment of migraine but fails to convey it is approved for the acute treatment of migraine and not indicated for preventive treatment.
cases.context: Full indication shown briefly in on-screen text at end only.
cases.rationale: Fails to adequately communicate full indication and limitations of use.
cases.check: Rule: indication statements must include 'acute' and the limitation of use when present in the PI.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Benefit claims in audio while risk information is text-only, small font, shown for four seconds at the end after the host says “we’ll be right back.”
cases.rationale: Risk presentation not comparable in prominence; placed where unlikely to draw attention.
cases.check: Rule: in video, risk must be narrated if benefits are narrated; flag risk shown after a closing cue or for very short durations.

cases.cat: Failure to submit at time of initial dissemination (Form FDA 2253)
cases.heading: Failure to Submit Under Form FDA-2253
cases.claim: A copy of the video was not submitted to OPDP under cover of Form FDA-2253 at the time of initial dissemination.
cases.check: Rule: confirm Form FDA 2253 submission at first use.
